content.text: Section 24 is squarely responsive, and no other clause creates a change-of-control right for Vendor (§ 9.x termination is insolvency-based only; § 13.3 confirms our licence-transfer right).

input.quote: 24.1 Customer may assign this Agreement or an Order Form without Vendor's consent to an Affiliate or to a successor in a merger, reorganization, acquisition, or sale of all or substantially all assets or business to which the Agreement relates.
input.rationale: Section 24 meets our preferred position on all material terms. 24.1 lets Customer assign to an Affiliate or to a merger/acquisition/substantially-all-assets successor without Vendor's consent (notice only); 24.2 bars Vendor assignment, delegation of material performance, or transfer by change of control without Customer's prior written consent, with a reasonableness standard running in our favour; 24.3 subjects other assignments to mutual consent not unreasonably withheld; and 24.4 expressly denies Vendor any right to terminate, suspend, reprice, accelerate Fees, or reduce service on Customer's change of control. No walk-away trigger exists, and § 13.3 confirms our licence rights travel with a permitted assignment. Two minor points short of ideal preferred wording, noted but not redlined: the competitor bar in 24.2 is limited to a "direct" competitor and is expressed as "without Customer's consent" rather than absolute — immaterial here because every Vendor assignment already requires our consent under the same sentence.
